edges.note: The released document names the programme itself. Its inside cover reads 'This product is one in a series of advanced technology reports produced in FY 2009 under the Defense Intelligence Agency ... Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications (AAWSA) Program' - the redaction between them is (b)(3):10 USC 424. Verified by downloading this DIRD and scanning its full text on 23 August 2026. The scans are OCR-degraded, so the quotation is normalised from the damaged rendering.

a.label: Cognitive Limits on Simultaneous Control of Multiple Unmanned Spacecraft

edges.label: subject domain: cognitive load limits on multi-vehicle control
edges.note: The commissioned question is how many unmanned vehicles a single human operator can control simultaneously - the human-factors constraint that would bound any swarming or multi-object control architecture. It forms a set with Genik's other two deliverables on limb-free control of external devices and on organic-molecule automation.

a.label: Cognitive Limits on Simultaneous Control of Multiple Unmanned Spacecraft

edges.label: authored by Richard J. Genik II
edges.note: The DIA list of 9 January 2018 records 'Cognitive Limits on Simultaneous Control of Multiple Unmanned Spacecraft, Dr R Genik, Wayne State Univ.' The released PDF's author block is redacted under (b)(6). Genik wrote three of the 38 DIRDs, the largest single-author block after Eric Davis's five.

a.label: Cognitive Limits on Simultaneous Control of Multiple Unmanned Spacecraft

edges.label: author's institution at time of writing
edges.note: Genik was director of the Emergent Technology Research Division and assistant professor in the Department of Psychiatry and Behavioral Neurosciences at the Wayne State University School of Medicine. Wayne State supplied four of the 38 DIRDs across two authors - Genik's three plus Kit Green's 'Field Effects on Biological Tissues' - the second-largest institutional concentration after EarthTech International's six.
